blocks.markdown: **Money laundering** is committed by any person who, **knowing that any monetary instrument or property represents, involves, or relates to the proceeds of any unlawful activity**: (a) transacts it; (b) converts, transfers, disposes of, moves, acquires, possesses, or uses it; (c) conceals or disguises its true nature, source, location, disposition, movement, ownership, or rights; (d) attempts or conspires to commit (a)–(c); (e) aids, abets, assists, or counsels (a)–(c); or (f) performs or fails to perform any act facilitating (a)–(c). Knowledge and the connection to unlawful proceeds must be established.

**Monetary instrument** covers specified currency and financial instruments — coins/currency, drafts, checks, notes, securities and similar instruments through which title can pass. **Person** means any natural or juridical person. **Proceeds** means an amount derived or realized from an unlawful activity. **Transaction** means an act establishing a right or obligation or a contractual/legal relationship, including any movement of funds by any means with a covered institution.

In plain English: money laundering is **not limited to physically carrying cash across borders**. Under Section 4 it can include transacting, converting, moving, acquiring, using, possessing, concealing, disguising ownership/source, attempting, conspiring, or helping another person do so — if the required knowledge and connection to unlawful proceeds are established.
Unlawful activities or predicate crimes: Section 3(i)

AMLA money laundering generally depends on **proceeds of any unlawful activity**. Section 3(i), as amended, lists predicate offenses including: kidnapping for ransom; dangerous-drugs offenses; specified anti-graft offenses and plunder; robbery/extortion; illegal gambling; piracy; qualified theft; swindling; smuggling; certain electronic-commerce and securities-law offenses; hijacking; terrorism and terrorism financing; bribery and corruption; frauds involving public funds; forgery/counterfeiting; trafficking; environmental/resource offenses involving forestry, fisheries, mining, wildlife and caves; carnapping; illegal firearms/explosives; fencing; specified migrant-worker offenses; intellectual-property offenses; photo/video voyeurism; child-protection offenses; strategic-trade-management violations involving weapons-of-mass-destruction proliferation financing; and specified serious tax crimes, subject to the statutory requirements.

**Study note:** the precise list and item numbering of Section 3(i) have been amended — use the **full current Section 3(i) text** linked in the sources. For recitation, be prepared to define what a predicate offense does: it is the **underlying unlawful activity whose proceeds may then be laundered**.

In plain English: think of two related but distinct wrongs — **(1) the predicate crime generates illegal proceeds; (2) the money-laundering offense involves dealing with those proceeds** in one of the ways listed in Section 4. The same person can be charged for both offenses when the law permits.
**Glossary — predicate offense:** the underlying unlawful activity whose proceeds may be the subject of money laundering.

title: Money laundering and predicate crimes
